ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that trapezoid $ABCD$ satisfies $AD \parallel BC$. The diagonal $AC$ intersects the midline $EF$ at point $G$. If $AD = 3$ and $EF = 5$, what is the length of $EG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $EF$ is the midline of trapezoid $ABCD$,\\
it follows that $CF=DF$,\\
and since $AD\parallel BC$,\\
it also follows that $\triangle CFG\sim \triangle CDA$,\\
thus $\frac{GF}{AD}=\frac{CF}{CD}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
therefore $GF=\frac{1}{2}AD=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
hence $EG=EF-GF=5-\frac{3}{2}=\boxed{\frac{7}{2}}$.

From the text, use AD=3 and EF=5. Since EF is the midline, F is the midpoint of CD and EF is parallel to AD and BC. Then in the right-side portion of the figure, compare triangles CFG and CDA: CF lies on CD, CG lies on CA, and GF is parallel to AD, so triangle CFG is similar to triangle CDA.
